page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a high-frequency compute server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz, the system provides 20 physical cores and 40 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache allocation consists of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2 per core, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, supporting AVX-512 VNNI instructions. System memory totals 192.0 GB, resulting in a density of 4.8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Networking features a 12 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while the hardware configuration includes no local SSD storage and zero GPU accelerators.

Across benchmark measurements, the instance operates within middle-tier performance distributions. In multi-core CPU evaluations, it records 38378.07 on stress-ng, 12045.0 on Geekbench, and 34691.95 on PassMark. Memory performance metrics show read bandwidth of 108.89 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside 34.78 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached persistent block storage, framing a primary architectural tradeoff between raw high-frequency processor execution and external storage latency.

The combination of 40 high-frequency dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB RAM positions the instance for compute-heavy parallel workloads. Key applicable deployment profiles include continuous integration software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, in-memory data caching, medium-scale database infrastructure, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It delivers 20 physical cores and 40 vCPUs with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX-512 VNNI instructions, 35 MB of L3 cache, KVM virtualization, and a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks locate its CPU and memory performance within average ranges, recording 38378.07 in stress-ng multi-core, 12045.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage and zero discrete GPUs, presenting a tradeoff that relies entirely on remote storage volumes. It is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, software compilation, database instances, and general application backends requiring stable multi-threaded processing.
